name: Opus Broadening
strategy: Broadening expressed where it is actually paying: an equal-weight and free-cash-flow value core, energy at full weight while WTI holds above $100 on the Hormuz premium, an AI-capex industrial sleeve, a regional-bank curve steepener, healthcare added as the defensive broadening leader, and precious metals cut to a single residual GLD hedge.
reassessment_note: Researched via WebSearch plus Yahoo daily closes through 10-30. Since the 10-26 rebalance the gold-break thesis that drove last week's metals trim has accelerated: gold futures fell from ~$4,075 (10-27) to ~$3,899 (10-30), -6.9% on the month and ~27% below January's record, and GDX fell 5.2% on 10-30 alone (-12.2% 1m). The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on 10-28 but with two hawkish dissents (Cook, Hammack) and futures price ~85% odds of a December hike, so real rates and a firm dollar (DXY ~102) remain a headwind; notably gold fell even as the 10-year eased from ~5.24% to 4.93% over the month, which says the haven bid is gone, not merely rate-suppressed. I am therefore exiting the higher-beta miners (GDX, 8%) rather than waiting for its -15% stop, and keeping GLD at 6% only as a tail hedge against a Hormuz re-escalation. 6% of the freed weight goes to XLV: on a week when SPY fell 0.56% and cap-weighted AI names cracked, healthcare rose 3.1% (+9.8% 1m), which is exactly the broadening rotation this book exists to own; the other 2% goes to cash at 4%. Everything else is unchanged and working: RSP +4.9% 1m, COWZ +6.9% 1m, XLE +13.9% 1m with WTI at $104, XLI flat-positive, and KRE only -1% (the curve steepened on FOMC day). Catalysts ahead: the 11-06 jobs report and 11-10 October CPI.

positions.thesis: Free-cash-flow value core: +6.9% over the past month while SPY is -0.9%, cash-generative balance sheets suit a regime where the Fed is pricing a December hike and 10-year yields sit near 5%. Kept at the largest weight because it is doing the book's job.
Equal-weight S&P is the purest broadening expression: +0.8% this week and +4.9% on the month against a falling cap-weighted SPY as AI-capex concentration unwinds. Unchanged at 16%.

WTI closed at $104 on 10-30 (+15% 1m) after Brent hit ~$117 on 10-23; energy CPI is +20% y/y and the Hormuz premium is still rebuilding despite on-off diplomacy. XLE +13.9% 1m; keep full weight with the 12% stop guarding against a diplomatic breakthrough.
Industrials capture AI-capex physical buildout and defense spending without megacap multiple risk; +1.7% this week while SPY fell. The Fed upgraded growth to 'strong'. Hold the trimmed 10% sleeve.

Regional banks as a curve-steepener: the 2s10s steepened on FOMC day (2-year ~4.70%, 10-year ~5.04%), widening net interest margins. Only -1% since entry; weak payrolls (29k) are the risk, sized at 8% with a 14% stop.

New leg replacing gold miners: healthcare is the leading defensive broadening sector, +3.1% this week and +9.8% on the month while SPY fell, and its earnings are insensitive to oil and rates. Sized at only 6% because it is entered after a strong run; 10% stop.

Residual tail hedge only: gold broke below $3,900 on 10-30 with a December hike priced, so no conviction long, but a 6% bullion position (lower beta than miners) protects against a Hormuz escalation or a Fed policy shock. The existing 10% stop from entry is the exit if the breakdown continues.
